Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Document-level info:
- Certificate number: R49/2006-SK1-14.02, Revision 1
- Member State: Slovakia
- Issuing Authority: Slovak Legal Metrology, Hviezdoslavova 31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia
- Person responsible: Jaromír Markovič (title: Ing. Jaromír Markovič, PhD.)
- Applicant: Ningbo Aimei Meter Manufacture Co., Ltd., 68, West Town Road, Shangtian Town, Fenghua City, Zhejiang, 315511 P.R. of China
- Manufacturer: The applicant
- Certified type: Mechanical multi-jet dry dial water meter for metering of cold water
- Type designations: MD-A; MD-AP
- Recommendation: R 49-1, edition 2006, accuracy class 2
- Date issued: 5 November 2014
- Test reports: 2013/MI-001/B075/001 (64 pages), 2014/MI-001/B041/312.03 (56 pages) — wait, note discrepancy: page 1 says "2014/MI-001/B041/312.03 having 56 pages" while section 7 says "Test report No 2014/MI-001/B041/001". I'll record both as they appear. The test reports section says:
  - Test report No 2013/MI-001/B075/001
  - Test report No 2014/MI-001/B041/001
  - Manufacturer's technical documentation stored in folder Ningbo_MD_A_00

Page total: 4 pages.

Date issued: 5 November 2014 (appears twice, likely issue date and CIML signature date).

Now the technical data. The certificate covers 6 nominal diameters: DN15, DN20, DN25, DN32, DN40, DN50. Each DN has 4 variants based on R ratio (Q3/Q1 = 80, 100, 125, 160). So the model family is DN × R ratio, giving up to 24 variants.

Table on page 2:

| DN=40: Q3 = 16 m³/h; Q1 ∈ {0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1}; Q2 ∈ {0.32, 0.256, 0.2048, 0.16}; Q4 = 20; Q3/Q1 ∈ {80,100,125,160}; Q2/Q1 = 1.6
| DN=50: Q3 = 25 m³/h; Q1 ∈ {0.3125, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15625}; Q2 ∈ {0.5, 0.4, 0.32, 0.25}; Q4 = 31.25; Q3/Q1 ∈ {80,100,125,160}; Q2/Q1 = 1.6

Then:
| DN (mm): 15, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50
| Connection thread: G ¾ B, G 1B, G11/4B, G11/2B, G2B, G2 1/2B / Flange ISO7005
| Construction length L (mm): 165/190, 190, 225/260, 230/260, 245/300, 280/300

| MPE upper flow rates range Q2 ≤ Q ≤ Q4 (%): ±2 (at Θ ≤ 30°C), ±3 (at Θ > 30°C)
| MPE lower flow rates range Q1 ≤ Q < Q2 (%): ±5
| Scale interval (m³): 0.00005
| Capacity of calculator (m³): 99999.99995
| Mechanical class: M1
| Climatic class (°C): -10 to +55

Now, how to structure this. The model family: models could be DN15..DN50 with attributes varying per DN, plus R ratio axis. The Q1 and Q2 values vary per both DN and R ratio.

Given the schema, I think the best approach:

- model_family.models: 6 models (DN15...DN50), model_id "DN15" etc.
- model_level characteristics:
  - permanent_flowrate_q3: per model
  - overload_flowrate_q4: per model
  - minimum_flowrate_q1: varies by DN × R — this is a config axis! Use config_level with axis "ratio_q3_q1" and condition "DN15,R80" etc. Or emit as config_level entries.
  - transitional_flowrate_q2: same.
  - ratio_q3_q1: config axis — but actually the R values {80,100,125,160} are the same for all DNs.
  
Alternative: treat each (DN, R) combination as a model variant — 24 variants. That may be cleaner for q1/q2 values. But 24 models is a lot. The schema example for R137 uses models per size. Here we have two dimensions: DN and R.

Hmm. Let me think about what's cleanest:

Option A: models = 6 DN variants. Config axis = "ratio_q3_q1" with conditions "R=80", "R=100", "R=125", "R=160". Then:
- model_level: q3, q4 per DN.
- config_level:
  - attribute minimum_flowrate_q1, axis "ratio_q3_q1 (per DN)", values: {condition: "DN15, R=80", value: 0.03125, unit m³/h}, ... 24 entries.
  - attribute transitional_flowrate_q2 similarly 24 entries.
  - ratio_q3_over_q1: condition values.
  - ratio_q2_over_q1: 1.6 constant (type_level? it's constant across all).

Actually q2/q1 = 1.6 is constant, so it can be type_level. And q3/q1 ∈ {80,100,125,160} for all DNs — config axis.

Option B: 24 models like "DN15-R80", "DN15-R100"... Then model_level has q1, q2, q3, q4 per model (24 values each), and matrix_tables preserves the original tables.

I think Option B is more faithful for a "model matrix" but Option A is more compact and captures the two-dimensional structure. The schema supports config_level exactly for this: "When attributes vary by configuration (not by model...)". Here R ratio is a configuration dimension of each DN model. I'll go with Option A: 6 models (DN-based), config_level for R-dependent attributes.

Actually wait — maybe better to do both: matrix_tables preserve the raw tables, model_level per DN for q3/q4/thread/length, config_level for q1/q2 per (DN, R).

Let me also consider matrix_tables: The original table is a multi-dim table. I could emit a matrix_table "Flow characteristics by nominal diameter and R ratio" with columns [dn, q3, q1_r80, q1_r100, q1_r125, q1_r160, q2_r80, ..., q4, ...]. Or rows per (DN, R) pair with columns dn, ratio_q3_q1, q1, q2, q3, q4. The latter is tidy: 24 rows. Let me do that.

Columns: ["nominal_diameter", "ratio_q3_q1", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "transitional_flowrate_q2", "minimum_flowrate_q1", "overload_flowrate_q4", "ratio_q2_q1"], column_units [mm, R, m³/h, m³/h, m³/h, m³/h, null].

Rows (24):
DN15: R80: q1=0.03125, q2=0.05, q3=2.5, q4=3.125, ratio=1.6

Wait, check DN40: "Minimum flowrate Q1: 0,2 0,16 0,128 0,1" and "Transitional flowrate Q2: 0,32 0,256 0,2048 0,16". R80 → q1 = q3/80 = 16/80 = 0.2 ✓. R160 → 16/160 = 0.1 ✓. q2 = 1.6 × q1: 0.32, 0.256, 0.2048, 0.16 ✓.

DN50: q3=25; R80: 25/80 = 0.3125 ✓; R100: 0.25 ✓; R125: 0.2 ✓; R160: 0.15625 ✓. q2: 0.5, 0.4, 0.32, 0.25 ✓.

DN32: q3=10; q1: 0.125, 0.1, 0.08, 0.0625 ✓; q2: 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1 ✓.

DN25: q3=6.3; q1: 0.07875, 0.063, 0.0504, 0.039375 ✓; q2: 0.126, 0.1008, 0.0864, 0.063 ✓.

Great.

Second matrix table: physical characteristics by DN:
Columns: nominal_diameter, connection_thread, construction_length (mm).
Rows:
- DN15: G ¾ B, 165/190
- DN20: G 1B, 190
- DN25: G11/4B, 225/260
- DN32: G11/2B, 230/260
- DN40: G2B, 245/300
- DN50: G2 1/2B / Flange ISO7005, 280/300

Construction length L: values like "165/190" — alternative lengths. I'll record as string "165/190" with unit mm. Or split min/max? It's alternatives, not a range. Keep as string. Actually per rules, values should be structured. `{value: "165/190", unit_symbol: "mm"}` — string values allowed when not numeric. Good.

model_level characteristics:
- nominal_diameter: DN15→15 ... DN50→50, unit mm
- permanent_flowrate_q3: 2.5, 4, 6.3, 10, 16, 25, unit m³/h
- overload_flowrate_q4: 3.125, 5, 7.875, 12.5, 20, 31.25, unit m³/h
- construction_length: strings per DN
- connection_thread: strings per DN

config_level:
- attribute minimum_flowrate_q1, axis "ratio_q3_q1 and nominal_diameter", values: 24 entries {condition: "DN15 @ R=80", value: 0.03125, unit m³/h}...

Hmm, but the config_level values shape per schema: `config_level[]: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}` and rule 5 says values follow `{condition, value, unit_symbol}`. So:

```json
{
  "attribute": "minimum_flowrate_q1",
  "axis": "nominal_diameter × ratio_q3_q1",
  "unit_symbol": "m³/h",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "DN15, R80", "value": 0.03125},
    ...
  ]
}
```

Actually the schema shows unit at the attribute level for model_level: `{"attribute": "qmax", "unit_symbol": "m³/h", "values": [...]}`. I'll put unit_symbol at attribute level for config_level too.

- ratio_q3_q1: attribute "ratio_q3_q1", axis "nominal_diameter", values: [{condition: "all DN", value: ...}] — no, it's {80,100,125,160} available for each DN. Hmm. Could emit as: attribute "ratio_q3_q1", axis "available_ratios", values [{condition: "DN15", value: {min:80,max:160}}]... no, that's a list. Maybe just record in the matrix table and as a config-level note. Or record type_level? No — it's a set.

Alternative approach: since ratio values are the axis itself, I can put ratio_q3_q1 as the axis name and not as a separate characteristic. But it might be worth recording as a characteristic with values listing options. Let me emit:

```json
{
  "attribute": "ratio_q3_q1",
  "axis": "nominal_diameter",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "DN15", "value": [80,100,125,160]}, ...
  ]
}
```

Hmm, value as list isn't in the allowed shapes (number | {min,max} | string). I could do value: "80/100/125/160" as string. Or better: emit it as part of the matrix table only, plus a type_level note? The rules say lists of values should be model matrices. Here it's the axis. I'll include it in matrix_tables (column ratio_q3_q1 in the tidy table) and add a config_level entry with string value "R80, R100, R125, R160" per DN. Actually, to keep it clean I'll skip a separate ratio characteristic since the axis name already conveys it, but the type_level could have... hmm.

Actually let me include it as config_level with string values to be explicit:

```json
{
  "attribute": "ratio_q3_over_q1_available_values",
  ...
}
```

That seems awkward. Alternatively treat R as a model attribute. Let me reconsider Option B more seriously.

Actually, thinking about downstream consumers: they'd probably want to query "for DN20 with R100, what is Q1?" A tidy matrix table with 24 rows handles this perfectly. The model_level per DN handles q3/q4. The config_level for q1/q2 per (DN × R) also handles it. I'll include all three but keep config_level for q1 and q2 only, since that's where the axis matters most.

For ratio_q3_q1 itself: values are {80,100,125,160} for all DNs — I'll record it as type_level? No, type_level must be single value. I'll record in config_level:

```json
{
  "attribute": "ratio_q3_over_q1",
  "axis": "nominal_diameter",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "DN15", "value": "80, 100, 125, 160"},
    ... all same
  ]
}
```

Hmm, or simpler: axis "nominal_diameter × available ratios". Actually, since the axis is literally the ratio, maybe I just describe the axis as "ratio_q3_q1" and don't add a redundant characteristic. The matrix table includes the ratio column. I think that suffices. But to be safe and explicit, I'll add a config_level entry with string value "R80/R100/R125/R160" for each DN. Actually let me keep it minimal — the axis name "ratio_q3_q1 (R)" makes it clear. Hmm, but the schema says axis describes the dimension, e.g. axis could be "nominal_diameter_and_ratio". 

Let me finalize:

config_level entries:
1. minimum_flowrate_q1, axis: "nominal_diameter × ratio_q3_q1", 24 values.
2. transitional_flowrate_q2, axis: "nominal_diameter × ratio_q3_q1", 24 values.
3. ratio_q2_over_q1 — constant 1.6 for all → type_level: ratio_q2_over_q1 = 1.6, unit null.
4. ratio_q3_over_q1 — available set; I'll include axis "nominal_diameter" with value "R80/R100/R125/R160" strings. Eh... I'll include it. Value as string "80/100/125/160". Fine.

type_level characteristics:
- installation_orientation: "H" (horizontal) — value string "H". Maybe "horizontal"? The table says "H". Keep "H". Hmm, value string "H (horizontal)"? Just "H".
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, °C. Note: "0,1 to 50" → decimal conversion 0.1 to 50.
- maximum_working_pressure: 16, bar.
- maximum_permissible_error_upper_flow_range: ±2% at Θ≤30°C and ±3% at Θ>30°C → config_level! Two conditions: {condition: "Θ ≤ 30 °C", value: -2 to +2? } Hmm, ±2 means ±2%. Value could be {min: -2, max: 2} with unit "%", condition "water temperature ≤ 30 °C". Yes, config_level with axis "water_temperature".

  ```json
  {
    "attribute": "maximum_permissible_error_upper_zone",
    "axis": "water_temperature",
    "unit_symbol": "%",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "Θ ≤ 30 °C", "value": {"min": -2, "max": 2}},
      {"condition": "Θ > 30 °C", "value": {"min": -3, "max": 3}}
    ]
  }
  ```
- maximum_permissible_error_lower_zone: ±5% → type_level: value {min: -5, max: 5}, unit "%".
- scale_interval: 0.00005 m³.
- capacity_of_calculator: 99999.99995 m³. (99999,99995 → 99999.99995)
- mechanical_class: "M1" (string).
- climatic_class: {min: -10, max: 55}, °C.
- accuracy_class: 2 — that's in recommendation.accuracy_classes though. Keep there.

Components: The description mentions essential parts: measuring mechanism, mechanical register (dry type), housing (brass for MD-A or plastic for MD-AP), adjustment device (if any), magnetic coupling. Optional non-essential: strainer, non-return valve; optional pulse output with reed sensor switch. Should these be components? They're sub-assemblies of the water meter. The rule says "include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies". The cert does name them. I could add components:
- role: "measuring_mechanism", description of impeller...
- role: "register" / "indicating device", type: "mechanical dry-type register, 5 digits, 4 pointers (6 digits for DN40/DN50)"
- role: "housing", alternatives? brass (MD-A) OR plastic (MD-AP) — alternatives "OR".
- role: "pulse_output" optional: "pulse output with reed sensor switch".

Hmm, components have role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics. These parts don't have type designations. I could include components with role and characteristics-free descriptions. Maybe keep it light:

```json
"components": [
  {"role": "measuring mechanism", "type_designations": [], "characteristics": {"description": "impeller with axle perpendicular to flow direction, lower and upper tightening plates with bearing hubs"}},
  {"role": "mechanical register", "characteristics": {"type": "dry type, digital drum with gearing mechanism", "digits": 5, "pointers": 4, ...}},
  ...
]
```

Hmm, characteristics is a free-form object in components? The schema shows `characteristics{}` for components — a dict. I'll use simple string/number values there (not the strict structured form, since rule 2 says "Every characteristic value" — that applies to characteristics section presumably. To be safe, I'll keep component characteristics simple strings).

Actually, to avoid over-engineering and risk of violating structured-value rules, I'll include components minimally:

- measuring mechanism
- register (dry type, 5 digits + 4 pointers; DN40/DN50: 6 digits + 4 pointers)
- housing: alternatives OR — brass body (MD-A) / plastic body (MD-AP)
- magnetic coupling
- optional: strainer, non-return valve, pulse output with reed sensor switch (optional)

Body material: brass for MD-A, plastic for MD-AP — this is a model-level attribute distinguishing the two types! model_family models: maybe 12 models = 2 types × 6 DNs? That's getting complex. The types MD-A and MD-AP differ only in body material. The DN×R matrix applies to both.

I'll handle: model_family.family_name: "MD-A / MD-AP". models: 6 DN models. And a type_level characteristic "housing_body_material": "brass (MD-A) / plastic (MD-AP)"? That's two values... config_level axis "type_variant": {condition "MD-A", value "brass"}, {condition "MD-AP", value "plastic"}. That fits config_level nicely.

Model ids: "DN15", "DN20", "DN25", "DN32", "DN40", "DN50". Labels could be "MD-A/MD-AP DN15" etc. Keep model_id simple.

Certificate level:
- number: "R49/2006-SK1-14.02"
- scheme: The schema says scheme (A|B). This is R49 under OIML-CS... 2014 certificate, likely scheme A? Actually OIML-CS Basic System started 2017; before that certificates were under the old system. The certificate doesn't state a scheme. Hmm. Rule 8: don't fabricate. The field "scheme (A|B)" — for older certificates, scheme isn't indicated. I'll omit it. Wait, but the certificate header says "OIML Certificate N°" — no scheme letter. I'll omit scheme.
- revision: "Revision 1" → revision_history: [{revision: "1", date: null?, changes: null}] — date not given for revision. Include revision_history with revision "1" and no date/changes? Rule 8 says omit if not present. revision_history entry needs revision (string). I'll include {"revision": "1"} — hmm, maybe date null. Actually the revision is part of the certificate number presentation. I'll include revision_history: [{"revision": "1", "date": null, "changes": null}]. Or omit entirely? The schema lists revision_history but if no info about changes... I'll include minimal entry since Revision 1 is clearly stated.

- project_number: not present. Omit.
- page_total: 4.
- member_state: "Slovakia".
- date_issued: "2014-11-05" (5 November 2014). Format — I'll use ISO "2014-11-05".
- oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly. Omit. (Slovakia's issuer... not stated in the doc. Omit.)

I'll set person_responsible: "Jaromír Markovič", person_title: null... Actually "The Issuing Authority / Ing. Jaromír Markovič, PhD." — his role title is the Issuing Authority representative. manufacturers: same as applicant ("The applicant"). Should I add manufacturers entry duplicating? The cert says "Manufacturer of the certified type: The applicant". I'll add manufacturers: [same entity] since it identifies the manufacturer. That's accurate, not fabrication.

certified_type:
- category: "Water meter" — the schema examples list categories; "Water meter" fits (examples show "Gas meter", "Measuring system"...). Use "Water meter".
- type_designations: ["MD-A", "MD-AP"]
- module_designation: null — not applicable (mechanical water meter, complete instrument). The schema: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For R49 water meters, module concept isn't used; set null or omit. I'll set null.
- description: "Mechanical multi-jet dry dial water meter intended for metering the volumes (consumption) of clean cold water in residential (households) and commercial use. Installed into pipe lines in horizontal installation positions."

recommendation:
- id: "R49" (canonical, not "R 49-1")
- edition: 2006
- amendment: null — omit.
- scheme: omit? The recommendation scheme... The schema has scheme under recommendation too. Certificate itself doesn't say A/B. Omit.
- accuracy_classes: [2] → wait, class is "2" for water meters per R49. accuracy_classes: ["2"] or [2]? Classes are typically strings like "R", but numeric 2 here. I'll use ["2"]... Hmm. Rule says numbers not strings for values. Accuracy class "2" — I'd emit as string "2" since it's a class designation. Actually class 2 is a metrological accuracy class per OIML R49 (class 2, being 2%). I'll use ["2"]. Hmm, or [2]. The schema example: accuracy_classes[]. For R49 the class is literally "Accuracy class 2". I'll emit ["2"] as strings since classes are designators. Actually, let me use ["2"]. Either is defensible.
